findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables, exposing long-lived IAM credentials to anyone with read access to the Terraform state, the function configuration, or the console.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so environment variables (which contain secrets here) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are visible in cleartext to any principal able to call GetFunctionConfiguration.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.

The function has no vpc_config block, so it runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL boundary, which eases exfiltration of the embedded credentials.
